successCriteria.description: The Notification domain interface is exported from the notification module and exposes the exact lifecycle union types: type ∈ {LEAVE_SUBMITTED, LEAVE_APPROVED, LEAVE_REJECTED, LEAVE_CANCELLED}, status ∈ {PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED}, relatedEntityType fixed to 'LeaveRequest', and readAt as Date | null.
The repository create operation persists a notifications row and returns a Notification whose status is 'PENDING' and readAt is null, regardless of any caller-supplied values for those fields.
findByRecipient returns all notifications for the given recipientId ordered newest-first (created_at DESC), and returns an empty array when the recipient has no notifications.

markAsSent transitions a notification's status to 'SENT' and markAsRead transitions status to 'READ' with readAt set to the current timestamp; both return null when no matching row exists and both are idempotent (re-marking an already-transitioned notification succeeds and re-stamps read_at on re-read).

createBatch inserts all provided notifications in a single multi-row INSERT and returns the persisted Notification array with every row defaulted to status 'PENDING' and readAt null; an empty input array returns [] without issuing any database query.

The notification module barrel re-exports the Notification model, the INotificationRepository interface, the CreateNotificationDto, and the NotificationRepository implementation class, so downstream modules import only through the module's public entry point.

The repository constructor accepts an optional Queryable client and defaults to the shared pg pool when none is provided, enabling the repository to participate in an outer transaction when a client is injected.

Jest unit tests in tests/unit/modules/notification/ cover create (PENDING forced, read_at null), findByRecipient (ordering, empty), markAsSent/markAsRead (transitions, null on missing, idempotency), createBatch (multi-row, empty array, PENDING default), and custom-client constructor injection — and the full suite passes.

constraints: No use of `any` — use `unknown` with type guards instead (HARNESS.json no-any, severity high). Strict TypeScript with strict null checks throughout the notification module.
All database access must go through the repository pattern (GP-001 / no-direct-db-outside-repository, severity critical) — no inline SQL or direct pool calls outside NotificationRepository.
Modules import from each other ONLY through their declared public entry point (index.ts barrel) — no imports of sibling module internals (AGENTS.md architecture rule 1).
SQL queries must use parameterized placeholders ($N) — no string-interpolated user input — to prevent SQL injection.
No unhandled promise rejections — all async repository errors must be caught and handled (GP-006).
outOfScope: NotificationService and its business logic (fanout orchestration, delivery scheduling) — owned by a later phase per the reconciled architecture module ownership.
Notification routes / API endpoints and RBAC enforcement on notification operations — no HTTP surface is part of this phase.
Database migrations / Knex schema definitions for the notifications table — this phase assumes the notifications table exists per the conceptual data model.
ARCHIVED status transition and any notification archiving/expiry logic — only PENDING→SENT and PENDING/SENT→READ transitions are exercised in this phase.

entityInvariants.invariant: A newly created Notification always begins its lifecycle in status 'PENDING' with readAt null — these are server-set initial-state fields that the repository enforces regardless of caller input; the create DTO must not carry them.

The status lifecycle is monotonic forward: PENDING → SENT → READ (ARCHIVED is a later-phase terminal state). markAsSent and markAsRead are idempotent — re-applying the same transition to an already-transitioned notification succeeds rather than failing, and re-reading re-stamps readAt to the current timestamp.

Every Notification is scoped to exactly one recipient (recipientId) and references exactly one related entity whose type is fixed to 'LeaveRequest' with a relatedEntityId — a notification cannot exist without this association.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Persists one notifications row with server-set status='PENDING' and read_at=NULL; returns the persisted Notification. Rejects (throws) on DB constraint violation. Caller-supplied status/readAt are ignored.
Returns all notifications for the recipient ordered by created_at DESC; returns [] when none exist. Read-only — never throws on missing recipient.
Sets status='SENT' for the matching row and returns the updated Notification; returns null when no row matches the id (not-found is a non-throwing outcome). Re-marking an already-SENT row succeeds.
Sets status='READ' and read_at=NOW() for the matching row and returns the updated Notification; returns null when no row matches the id. Re-marking an already-READ row succeeds and re-stamps read_at.

Inserts all provided notifications in a single multi-row INSERT, each defaulted to status='PENDING' and read_at=NULL, and returns the persisted array in insertion order. An empty input array short-circuits to [] without a DB round-trip. Throws on DB constraint violation.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The Notification entity shape (fields, union types, nullability) must match the authoritative definition in the reconciled architecture — type union of 4 leave-event values, status union of PENDING/SENT/READ/ARCHIVED, relatedEntityType fixed to 'LeaveRequest', readAt: Date | null.

The repository must follow the Transaction Contract: constructor accepts an optional Queryable (Pick<Pool,'query'>) client defaulting to the shared pool, so repository methods can join a caller's outer transaction when a client is passed. This matches the established pattern in sibling repositories.

The repository's row-mapping convention (private snake_case Row interface + rowToNotification mapper + shared COLUMNS constant isolating DB column names from the domain layer) must match the established convention used by the leave-balance repository.

The createBatch empty-array short-circuit (return [] without a query) and single multi-row INSERT with dynamic $N placeholders must match the established createBatch convention in sibling repositories.

The notifications table column layout referenced by the repository (recipient_id, type, title, message, related_entity_type, related_entity_id, status, created_at, read_at) must match the conceptual data model declared in the reconciled architecture.

integrationPoints.why: The repository defaults to the shared pool for standalone queries and must import it as the fallback Queryable when no client is injected.

The notification repository is consumed by the future LeaveRequestService to fan out notifications (LEAVE_SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED) to employees and managers on lifecycle transitions, including within the approval-flow transaction.

Downstream modules (leave-request) must import Notification, INotificationRepository, CreateNotificationDto, and NotificationRepository only through this public entry point per the module-boundary rule.
